coverage.description: The normative requirements of ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025, clauses 3 to 7 and the normative annexes (A, B, C, H to N), paraphrased, with the cases that cover each. Annex D is informative; its items are listed because 6.3 refers to it.

requirement.text: An abstract rule does not fire by itself.
Only the patterns of the active phase are used.
Patterns have no defined order; pattern and group are patterns.
A pattern may belong to several phases; #ALL, #ANY, #DEFAULT are reserved.
A rule context matches a node not matched by a lexically earlier rule of the same pattern.
The subject is the node a finding is about.
Valid means every assertion test of the fired rules of active patterns passes.
A variable is scoped to the schema, phase, pattern or rule that declares it.
A schema is a well-formed XML 1.0 or 1.1 document.
Schematron elements are in the Schematron namespace; the prefix is free.
Foreign attributes and foreign child elements are allowed anywhere.
Whitespace-only text children are allowed anywhere.
Strip whitespace around attribute values; collapse whitespace in text.
A schema follows the grammar of Annex A.
active names a pattern active in the phase.
An assert succeeds when its test is true; it needs a test.
The natural-language assertion is a positive statement.
requirement.untested: A matter of the schema's prose; no processor can check it.

requirement.text: flag, role, subject, severity, icon, see, fpi on assert.
extends has an href or a rule attribute, not both.
extends rule names an abstract rule, whose assertions the rule uses.
extends href names an element of the parent's kind (schema, library, rule) whose contents replace it.
Errors while processing extends are reported; termination is implementation-defined.
group is a pattern without if-then-else: every matching rule fires.
include href names a well-formed document or one of its elements.
The included element replaces include and must be allowed there.
Errors while processing include are reported; termination is implementation-defined.
A rule variable uses the rule's context; others use the document root.
value is an expression; without it the element content is the value.
The binding decides whether and how as is processed.
Referencing an undefined variable is an error.
A variable defined more than once over schema, phase, pattern and rule is an error.
Variables are substituted into tests and other expressions of the rule.
A library holds external declarations brought in by extends.
name gives the name of the node path selects, else of the context node.
ns prefix is a name without a colon; uri is required.
Prefixes in queries are defined by ns, not by XML namespace declarations.
A schema param needs a value; its value may be overridden by the user.
An instance's param value, else the abstract param's, is used; no value is an error.
Parameter names and number correspond between abstract and concrete patterns.
Parameter names are distinct within a pattern or schema.
documents is evaluated at the instance root; the pattern is sought only in those documents, resolved against the instance's base URI.
Pattern variables are not in scope in documents.
A document that cannot be retrieved is reported.
Subordinate documents are retrieved deterministically.
requirement.untested: Not observable in a single run.

requirement.text: An abstract pattern has an id and no is-a.
A phase names a set of active patterns; it needs an id.
#ALL, #ANY and #DEFAULT are not phase names; their meanings.
A report succeeds (is a finding) when its test is true.
A report's text states a found pattern or a negated constraint.
requirement.untested: A matter of the schema's prose; no processor can check it.

requirement.text: A rule needs a context unless it is abstract; an abstract rule has none.
A rule that never fires is not an error.
rules holds abstract rules for use across patterns, at schema or library level.
schema is the top element; defaultPhase names the phase used without user choice.
value-of select is evaluated in the current context and gives a string.
The assertion's variables are in scope in its diagnostics.
diagnostics links an assertion to diagnostic elements.
dir is text with a direction ltr or rtl.
emph encloses emphasized text.
A flag becomes true when an assertion with it fails or a rule with it fires.
A flag that is a variable reference is evaluated.
from is evaluated at the instance root and restricts rule contexts to what it selects.
from does not apply to subordinate documents.
p is documentation.
The assertion's variables are in scope in its properties.
role names the function of an assertion or rule.
A role that is a variable reference is evaluated.
schematronEdition, where given, is 2025.
The edition or its absence is reported at user option.
severity names an assertion's importance; fatal, error, warning, info are reserved.
A severity that is a variable reference is evaluated.
span encloses text keyed by a class.
subject is evaluated in the rule's context; without it the context node is used.
title is documentation.
visit-each selects the contexts of the assertions; if empty the rule still fires.
when is evaluated at the instance root; the first true phase in schema order is active.
when does not apply to subordinate documents.
Validation returns valid, invalid or error, given binding, schema, instance, documents, phase and parameters.
Inclusions, abstract patterns and abstract rules are resolved, reports negated, documentation removed.
The phase is established first, then each active pattern is processed.
A rule of a pattern fires unless an earlier rule matched the node; in a group every rule may fire.
Each assertion of a fired rule is evaluated for each matched node.
name and value-of in a message use the assertion's subject, else the rule's subject, else the rule context.
An instance has no rules and a param for each parameter used.
Parameter values replace the references in the abstract pattern.
A binding provides the query language, its rule-context language and the assertion test.
requirement.untested: A requirement on binding specifications, not on processors.

requirement.text: A binding specifies whitespace processing of queries and restrictions on names.
requirement.untested: A requirement on binding specifications; struct-whitespace exercises the whitespace in queries.

requirement.text: An implementation that does not support the schema's binding fails with an error.
Reserved binding names are matched in any mix of case.
Without queryBinding the default binding xslt (Annex C) applies.
xslt2, xpath2, xslt3, xpath3, xpath31, xquery3, xquery31 follow Annexes H to N.
Order of elements, patterns and assertions is implementation-dependent; only rules in a pattern and lets are ordered.
Rules act as if-then-else in a pattern, not in a group.
A let may use earlier variables of its rule and global variables.
Queries act as pure functions and do not change the instance.
requirement.untested: The standard XPath and XSLT query languages have no side effects to observe.

requirement.text: Language fixup when incorporating include and extends and instantiating.
Base URI fixup when incorporating include and extends.
A simple-conformance implementation reports that a document does not conform.
A schema conforms to Annexes A and B.
Validity is determined for any document and schema.
Incorrectness the query language establishes is reported.
A full-conformance implementation determines whether a document is a correct schema.
One definition per variable name in the global and the local context.
flag, id, name and prefix are well-formed names.
The schema's children come in the grammar's order.
At most one diagnostics and one properties element.
id is of type ID: unique, and a well-formed name.
diagnostics, properties, defaultPhase, active pattern and extends rule refer to existing ids.
Elements appear only where the grammar allows them.
Required attributes are present (test, context, select, class, uri, id).
active/@pattern matches a pattern id.
extends/@rule matches an abstract rule.
A variable and an abstract pattern parameter do not share a name.
Parameter names are unique in their scope.
is-a matches an abstract pattern's id.
An instance's param names match the abstract pattern's params.
An instance param has a value, its own or the abstract's.
A schema param has a value.
No queryBinding or xslt (any case) uses the XSLT 1.0 binding.
Text nodes as context at user option.
$ followed by a parameter name marks a parameter; otherwise it is not one.
XSLT import, include, key before patterns; copy-of in property; AVTs for flag, role, severity.
requirement.untested: Covered for the xslt2 and xslt3 bindings; the XSLT 1.0 binding is read as each implementation chooses (binding-xslt-version-sensitive).

requirement.text: The query language is XPath 2.0 or 3.x as in XSLT, without backwards compatibility.
The rule context is an XSLT pattern: root, elements, attributes, comments, PIs; text nodes at user option.
The test is reduced to its effective Boolean value.
name uses fn:node-name of what path selects.
value-of uses fn:string of what select returns.
A let is an XSLT variable; as follows XSLT's rules.
documents returns strings read with document().
$name marks a parameter only when name is an in-scope parameter.
xsl:function, key, include, import, import-schema, use-package, accumulator before patterns.
xsl:copy-of without children inside property.
Attribute value templates for flag, role and severity.
Text value templates in messages.
The query language is XPath of that version, with no user-written functions.
The rule context is an XPath expression selecting elements, attributes, comments, PIs.
Rule contexts are evaluated from the document node; text nodes are allowed.
How XQuery declarations and imports are included.
SVRL: schematron-output, active-pattern, fired-rule, failed-assert, successful-report.
The mapping of Table D.1: phase, title, ns, diagnostics, properties, groups, documents.
